reading: bits per UTF-8 byte of the held-out rows train.py holds out, decoded to text so both arms score the SAME bytes with their own tokenizers
boundary: NOT comparable to domain_loss.py's numbers: that metric is nats per TOKEN and every existing record and threshold is in those units. This is a second reading for the cross-tokenizer comparison, not a replacement. The mean is unweighted over the domains that produced a number; `skipped` names the rest with reasons, since a mean over a silently smaller set is a different metric wearing the same name.
